text:
B: Hello, love! Can you hear me? I'm Marijke.
A: Hi! Yeah, I can hear you. I'm Megan. Sorry, I've been waiting to talk to you, actually. That sounds weird.
B: Waiting for me? Why, what have they said?
A: No, nothing bad! Just, erm, when I saw your photo you reminded me of my nan. In a nice way. She's really warm and she's always got biscuits out.
B: Ha! Well, I have got the biscuit tin, you can see it there. Dutch ones, from my sister. So I'm the nan of the group, that's fine. Zain said I'm a dinner lady.
A: Oh no, that's funny. My mum's a dinner lady, so I'd take that as a compliment, honestly.
B: Is she? Then it's good. What do you do, love, are you working?
A: I'm at uni, second year. Wildlife and conservation. So like birds and ponds and li'le mammals, that kind of thing.
B: Ah, the bird girl. Jade told me about you, I think. With the chart.
A: Ha, yeah. Everyone knows me as the bird girl now. Erm, it's kind of my nan's fault, really. She's got an allotment in Harlow, and when I was li'le I'd go down with her every weekend and she'd tell me what all the birds were. Robins following the spade, blackbirds pinching the strawberries. And I just never stopped looking, do you know what I mean? I still help her when I go home on Sundays.
B: That's nice, that's very nice. I only do my hanging baskets, the rest is Keith. They did very well this year, the baskets. Petunias, trailing ones, all down the front.
A: Oh, lovely. Do you get bees on them?
B: Yes, lots. Big fat ones.
A: Bumblebees, probably. That's really good for them, honestly.
B: Well, there you go, I'm helping and I didn't know.
A: Ha, exactly. Erm, sorry, what do you do? I should've asked first.
B: Carer. Mornings, I go to people's houses, I get them washed and dressed, breakfast, tablets. Finish by eleven.
A: That's so nice. I think I'd like that, kind of. I'm good with old people. And animals. Not so good with the stats bit of my course.
B: Stats, I don't even know what that is. What else, erm... where's home for you?
A: Chelmsford now, with my boyfriend. But my mum and my brother are in Harlow, about forty minutes. I feel a bit bad sometimes, moving away from them.
B: Forty minutes! I moved to another country, love. Forty minutes is nothing. You go every Sunday, you said?
A: Most Sundays, yeah.
B: Then you're a good girl. Your mum's fine. I ring my sister every Sunday, it's the same thing.
A: Yeah. Yeah, I suppose that's true. Thank you.
B: Do you go to the charity shops? You look like a charity shop girl.
A: Oh my god, all the time. I got this hoodie in one.
B: I knew it! I got a cardigan in the hospice shop last week, three pounds, still had the label.
A: Three pounds! That's amazing.
B: I think we're nearly finished. Say hello to your nan from the other nan.
A: Ha, I will. She'll love that.
